nodes.label: Chrono::ROS two-process architecture
nodes.rationale: The simulation process holds NO ROS symbols and the ROS node process holds NO Chrono physics symbols, communicating only over IPC. This exists to avoid symbol conflicts, particularly between VSG visualization and ROS 2 libraries as of Chrono 9.0. The interface reserves at least 1GB of /dev/shm to support 4K Chrono::Sensor image transport, so Docker's default 16MB SHM must be overridden.

nodes.label: Handler concept (bridge across the process boundary)
nodes.rationale: A complete handler is four files: ChROS<Name>Handler.h/.cpp in the main process (extraction + serialization), ChROS<Name>Handler_ipc.h shared by both, and ChROS<Name>Handler_ros.cpp in the subprocess (ROS publish/subscribe).

nodes.label: Shared IPC header contract (*_ipc.h)
nodes.rationale: Described as the most critical file: it is the contract between the two processes, so it must contain only POD structs - no pointers, no std::string/std::vector or other dynamic containers, and no ROS or Chrono headers. Variable-length payloads (e.g. camera pixels) follow the struct in the byte stream and fixed-size char arrays stand in for strings.

nodes.label: ChROSHandler base class
nodes.rationale: Handlers subclass it and override Initialize, GetMessageType and GetSerializedData; bidirectional handlers additionally override HandleIncomingMessage and SupportsIncomingMessages. ChROSManager is generic and needs no modification for a new handler type.

nodes.label: Publisher pattern (Chrono to ROS)
nodes.rationale: One-way flow for sensors and state reporting: extract from the Chrono object, memcpy into the IPC struct, return a byte vector; the subprocess reinterpret_casts it, lazily creates a publisher in a static topic-keyed map, and publishes.

nodes.label: Subscriber pattern (ROS to Chrono)
nodes.rationale: Bidirectional two-phase flow: GetSerializedData sends the topic name exactly once as a setup message that causes the subprocess to create the subscription, after which the ROS callback packs control data and sends it back over the stored IPCChannel for HandleIncomingMessage to apply to the Chrono object.

nodes.label: ipc::MessageType enum registration
nodes.rationale: A unique MessageType id in src/chrono_ros/ipc/ChROSIPCMessage.h is what lets the subprocess dispatch an incoming byte blob to the right registered callback - it is the discriminator of the IPC wire format.

nodes.label: Handler registration build-system pitfall
nodes.rationale: CHRONO_ROS_REGISTER_HANDLER only runs if the _ros.cpp is compiled into the chrono_ros_node target. Forgetting to add it to target_sources still compiles cleanly but produces runtime 'No handler registered for message type' warnings, because the registration macro never executes in the subprocess.

nodes.label: Optional SWIG registration for PyChrono
nodes.rationale: Exposing a handler to Python requires three edits in src/chrono_swig/interface/ros/ChModuleROS.i: the C++ include, a %shared_ptr declaration, and a %include of the header.

nodes.label: Handler throttling and buffer-reuse best practice
nodes.rationale: GetSerializedData should rate-limit using m_update_rate and return an empty vector when it is not time to publish, because simulation can run many times faster than realtime and would otherwise overload the DDS middleware. Buffers should be reused member variables rather than per-call vector allocations.
